//: Manifest ∩ grant conformance cases, read by BOTH languages.
//why: The Dart client and the Rust host both resolve what a mini app holds. If
they resolved it differently, an app would hold one set of capabilities on
a phone and another on the server, and the difference would surface only as
a bug in whichever direction was more permissive.
This file is the shared source of truth. Rust reads it in
test/policy_conformance_test.dart. A case added here must pass in both.
Capability names are wire names (Capability::as_str / ElpianCapability.wireName).
A null limit means unbounded on that axis.

cases.name: an empty request means everything granted
cases.why: An app that simply omitted the field would otherwise launch with no capabilities and fail confusingly. Least privilege applies to what an app states, not to what it forgot to state.

cases.name: a request narrower than the grant is honoured
cases.why: Least privilege: a generous grant does not push capabilities onto an app that did not ask.

cases.name: a request wider than the grant is cut down, and the excess is reported
cases.why: The security direction. The denied set exists so an app can be told exactly what it did not get.

cases.name: an unknown capability name is dropped, not rejected
cases.why: A manifest written against a newer Elpian must not brick the app on an older host, and dropping can only narrow what is asked for.

cases.name: limits intersect axis by axis, tighter wins
a null axis means unbounded from that side, so the other wins
cases.why: NOT min-on-Option, which would let an app widen its budget by omitting an axis.

cases.name: null on both sides stays null
no requested limits at all means the grant's budget applies
hosting children needs all three of request, grant and vm_manage
hosting children is refused without the grant
hosting children is refused without the manifest asking
hosting children is refused without vm_manage surviving the intersection
cases.why: The capability is the mechanism; asking and being allowed are not enough if the gate itself was not granted.

cases.name: an empty request with a vm_manage grant can still host children
cases.why: The empty-request rule means the app is treated as requesting everything granted, so vm_manage is held.

cases.name: the surface capability resolves on both sides
cases.why: It was missing from the Dart enum entirely while the VM had it, so godot.op and flutter.op fell through to the catch-all gate.

cases.name: the server-side capabilities resolve on both sides
